Hi Maria — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, details below:

- No training on customer content (hosted API) unless the customer explicitly opts in to data sharing.
- Request logs are retained for 90 days by default; debugging snapshots (operational traces) are retained up to 30 days before tombstoning and then purged within 180 days unless retained for an outstanding support/legal hold.
- KV caches and per-request ephemeral state are not persisted beyond the inference session; they are cleared immediately after the request completes.
- Encrypted backups (used for disaster recovery) are retained up to 365 days to meet operational SLAs; backups are encrypted and access-controlled.

A few clarifications and items that matter for contracts:

1) "No training" scope: this covers model weight updates and inclusion of customer content in any training dataset we use to update production models. It applies to our hosted service. For Redwood Dedicated and Redwood Private, customers can opt for configurations that further isolate telemetry and disable outbound telemetry entirely.

2) Tombstone definition: when we 'tombstone' a debug snapshot we render the data logically inaccessible in the product and remove it from active indexes; tombstoned artifacts are retained in encrypted storage for forensics or legal hold until final purge. 'Final purge' means secure deletion from primary stores and overwriting (per our deletion playbook) — typically completed within 180 days of tombstone unless a hold is in place.

3) SRE/Engineer access: access to raw customer content for debugging is rare, logged, and requires an elevated access justification (ticket + manager approval). We use masked tooling where possible. Audits and SOC2 controls apply.

4) Deletion requests: we support an API/portal request to delete customer content; for hosted customers this triggers tombstone + purge workflow. For Dedicated customers we offer configurable retention windows as part of the contract.

Hi Maria — adding a legal nuance that often comes up in procurement language: our "no training" commitment is contractual and excludes cases where a customer has explicitly agreed to share usage data for model improvement. We also make an exception for aggregated telemetry that is fully de-identified and non-attributable, which we generally use only to monitor platform health (not to improve model outputs).

If you need contract language, we can provide a short clause that states: "Supplier shall not use Customer Content to train, fine-tune, or otherwise update machine learning models used in production, except where Customer has given explicit, written consent."

Also note: for customers subject to regulatory retention (e.g., financial services), we can configure extended retention or hold policies — these are handled via the Dedicated/Private offerings and reflected in the order form.
